object_description: two angled three-storey cubes following the street with a recessed gymnasium
design_condition: the two volumes follow the street at a slight angle so that the larger one opens a break area reading as a widening of the existing path axis, with the arrangement following the course of the stream

positive: Angling the larger building creates a successful open space and break area for meeting and viewing the existing complex
It can be read as a widening of the existing path axis
Tree islands set into the paved surface link to the water area and its front zone
The arrangement follows the course of the stream and forms an attractive natural strip
The three-storey cubes have a clear connection to the volumes of the neighbouring settlement
The connection to the existing school complex is directly guaranteed by bicycle and pedestrian paths
The all-weather pitch on the gymnasium roof makes an important contribution to play and recreation
The two open spaces visually integrate the existing school complex into the project
The angles towards the street are considered desirable
The spatial relationships are clearly defined and designated by three entrances
The different school types are clearly arranged over the two levels
The orientation of the school use is correct
The multi-storey inner courtyard at the pivot point provides natural lighting
Day and evening operation is possible without any problems
Access areas and stairwells are clearly arranged and correspond to problem-free school operations
The classrooms are adequately lit and the outdoor area is described as very good
The foyer and learning landscape are open on two floors with the main staircase naturally lit from above
The prefabricated timber system construction with concrete cores is coherent
Micropiles and pile foundations protect against buoyancy without impairing groundwater flow
The lightness of the volumes and facade corresponds to the flanking buildings and should lead to acceptance
negative: The rooftop pitch can hardly create the necessary overlap of use with the other outdoor areas
Access to the sports hall is narrow and would have to be widened
The day structure does not form a single unit, as toilets and kitchen lie outside it
This is considered problematic for operational reasons
Bonded roofs are alien to the region
A shingled wooden facade should be questioned
